item.title: As U.S. bombs Iran, Pope Leo criticizes those who would use God for war
item.summary: Some Trump administration officials cloak the war on Iran in religious terms, but the Chicago-born pope said that God “does not listen to the prayers of those who wage war.”

item.title: As Trump doubles down on Iran war, markets shudder and oil prices climb
item.summary: Britain’s Keir Starmer hosts a meeting of world leaders for talks on the waterway amid mounting pressure from the Trump administration to join the Iran war.

item.title: Israelis celebrate Passover in a parking garage turned bomb shelter
item.summary: People broke matzoh, read from the Haggadah and sang — with no need to worry about when the next air raid siren might sound.

item.title: Migrant workers keep Dubai running but can’t afford to flee Iranian strikes
item.summary: As Iran’s retaliatory attacks hit regional centers of commerce, such as Dubai, the majority of the deaths have been among migrant workers who could not afford to flee.

item.title: Wartime fuel shortages spawn panic, robberies and killings in Asia
item.summary: Gas is being stolen, and station workers in Bangladesh, Pakistan and India have been killed over shortages and high prices. Unrest is set to worsen the longer the war lasts.

item.title: Risky commando plan to seize Iran’s uranium came at Trump’s request
item.summary: A plan briefed to Trump last week to insert ground forces to remove Iran’s nuclear material would be a very difficult endeavor of a type never before attempted in wartime.

item.title: Trump heralds regime change, but Iran’s leaders remain hard-liners
item.summary: The president says Iran’s remaining leaders are more reasonable. But assassinations have left in place an emboldened government driving a hard bargain, officials say.

item.title: Sudanese rebels used rape as a weapon, aid group says
item.summary: Sexual violence is a widespread weapon of war in Sudan. “Survivors frequently and clearly identified the perpetrators as RSF fighters,” Doctors Without Borders says.

item.title: American journalist Shelly Kittleson kidnapped in Baghdad
item.summary: Iraq’s interior ministry said it had arrested one suspect, seized a car and was looking for accomplices.

item.title: Cuba says it will release over 2,000 prisoners, as U.S. keeps up pressure
item.summary: The move, described by the communist government as a “humanitarian and sovereign gesture,” comes as the U.S. enforces a crippling oil blockade on the island.
